headline: Public hearings on utility conduits at 116 and 124 Rodney St. and on FY27 tax rates, plus a draft public camping ordinance.
summary: Twenty petitions cover zoning, streets, traffic, and parks, and they go to committees. The agenda also lists FY27 tax and budget items, three grants, appointments, and a draft public camping ordinance.
items: Public hearing and order granting National Grid a conduit location at 116 Rodney St.
Public hearing and order granting National Grid a conduit location at 124 Rodney St.
Public hearing to set FY27 tax rates for residential, commercial, industrial, and personal property
City Manager reports on two proposed FY27 tax classification rules, an FY27 tax rate FAQ, and two proposed FY27 budget adjustments
City Manager order on the Elderly Exemption Program
Petition to rezone 9 Alvarado Ave. into the BL-1.0 zone and the Commercial Corridors Overlay district, referred to Planning Board
Petition to set a 5,000 square foot minimum lot and 50 feet of frontage for single-family homes in RS-10, RS-7, and RL-7, referred to Planning Board
Petitions for street and sidewalk resurfacing and a streetlight on Wildwood Ave., Fairhaven Rd., Southbridge St., and Coburn Ave., referred to Public Works Committee
Petitions for traffic studies, speed humps, parking zones, stop signs, crosswalks, and signs, referred to Traffic and Parking Committee
Petitions for pickleball courts at South Worcester Playground and renovation of the Logan Field basketball court, referred to Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation Committee
Set hearings for November 24, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. on an Eversource gas main on Wigwam Ave. and a National Grid conduit on Dewey St.
Appointment of Michelle Glaser to the Commission for the Preservation of Historic Artifacts, Relics, and Military Memorials
Appointment of Ettore "Frank" Torti to the Worcester Housing Authority

Public Works reports on Juniper Road and Olean Street stormwater review, a private plow rate increase, winter program update, Keep Worcester Clean update, and October 2026 street and sidewalk progress
Grant acceptances: $14,000 from MassDOT, $30,000 for police bulletproof vests, and $59,649.32 for traffic enforcement
Raise the FY27 spending limit for Library Book Replacements to $100,000
Authorize payment of three prior year invoices totaling $3,980.07
Report on the "Disrupting the Cycle" strategic framework for unhoused individuals and recommendation to adopt a draft Public Camping Ordinance
Items held under privilege: Belmont St. zoning petition, rodeo draft ordinance, bicycle and e-bike safety order, and World War II Museum artifacts order
Tabled items, including a legal opinion on rent control, an Office of Housing Stability order, and an equity audit order
Orders from November 10 under suspension of rules: Roosevelt Elementary pickup report (denied), speed hump installation process report (adopted), and drone tracking report (adopted)
location: Esther Howland (South) Chamber, City Hall, 455 Main Street, Worcester, Massachusetts

Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the 
impersonation of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting 
payments be made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions . 
All official emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an 
@worcesterma.gov email address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical 
mail on the City of Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will 
always include your specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date , 
time, and location. The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.
